html:
A Japanese industrialist who founded the company now called Panasonic in Osaka, and who is known in Japan as the god of management.

He left school at nine to work as an apprentice and later at the Osaka electric light company. In 1918 he started his own firm at home with his wife and her brother, making an improved two way light socket. Bicycle lamps, radios and irons followed. He believed a maker's mission was to make goods as plentiful and cheap as tap water, and he set up a structure of separate divisions, unusual in Japan at the time.

After the war the American occupation first restricted him as a wartime industrialist, then lifted the ban. In the boom years his company made the televisions, washing machines and fridges that filled Japanese homes, under brands such as National. He was famed for lifetime employment and treating workers as family. Late in life he founded a school to train young political leaders. He sits with the founders of Sony and Toyota among Japan's model entrepreneurs.
sum: A Japanese industrialist who founded the company now called Panasonic in Osaka, and who is known in Japan as the god of management.
